newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Adopted children testify in Austria abuse trial.
newsitem.headline: Adopted children testify in Austria abuse trial.

text.p: A former foster child of an Austrian woman accused of locking her retarded daughter in a coffin-shaped box for days on end said on Friday she too had been abused and often locked up by her mother.
Another adopted daughter told a Vienna court she had witnessed the abuse but did nothing about it.
The mother, a former religious education teacher, named only as Ernestine K., 65, is charged with instigating the abuse of her retarded adopted daughter Maria, now 22.
Her husband Walter is also accused of abuse and incarceration, while family friend Irmengard M. is accused of being an accomplice.
The couple had adopted or fostered seven children over the years.

Dorit J., 43, the first foster child in the family, recently wrote a book entitled "The Unwanted Child" in which she claims she was frequently locked in the toilet or the living room and tied to the coffee table.
In court Dorit said: "She (Ernestine) ruled the roost. She decided and ruled everything. She was a very quick-tempered person."
Sabine, 26, who was adopted as a child by the couple, testified that she had witnessed the abuse of Maria and watched her suffer for about 10 years.
"I was a coward...I studied and had a nice life. But I did not want to be an accomplice to murder," she said.
Last year, Sabine alerted the Vienna authorities to Maria's ordeal in an anonymous letter and the girl was taken away from the family's home in a Vienna suburb.
But three other adopted children who appeared as witnesses said they knew very little about allegations of Maria being locked in a box and denied she had undergone any suffering.
The wooden box was found smeared with excrement and urine and contained blood-stained newspapers inside, prosecutors said.

Chief prosecutor Michael Klackl alleges Ernestine beat Maria and frequently locked her in a garden shed with her hands tied together and her mouth sealed with sticking plaster when the couple went out.
Ernestine denied all the charges except that of locking Maria in the box, saying she had hoped it would make her undersized daughter grow.

The wooden box, measuring 160 cm by 55 cm and 33 cm deep, (64 inches by 22 and 13.2 deep) with 14 holes for air and a bolt on the outside, was displayed in court on the first day of the trial on Wednesday.
Maria who is undergoing psychiatric treatment, said in a video testimony played in court on Wednesday, that she had been terrified of "Mummy".
Asked what "Mummy" used to do, she said: "She beat me, kicked me in the stomach, pulled my ears and tore my hair."
If convicted, Ernestine and her husband could face up to 10 years in jail.
